newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CHELSEA HIT BY BOARDROOM RESIGNATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHELSEA HIT BY BOARDROOM RESIGNATION.

text.p: English premier league club Chelsea, rocked by the death of vice-chairman and benefactor Matthew Harding last month, faced fresh boardroom turmoil on Thursday after director Peter Middleton quit the club.
A statement from the club said only that Middleton had resigned as a director of both the soccer club and the Chelsea Village holding company which owns it.

Middleton, who heads the European operation of the American investment firm Salomon Brothers, had been tipped to play a more prominent role at the club following the death of his friend Harding in a helicopter accident.
Harding was among five people who died when the helicopter carrying them back to London after Chelsea's League Cup defeat by Bolton came down in north-west England.
Middleton, former chief executive of the Lloyd's insurance market, had been due to make the trip with Harding but withdrew at the 11th hour because of a speaking engagement.

Harding had poured around 20 million pounds ($33 million) of his own personal fortune into Chelsea and owned a stake of around 25 percent in the club. But he had a series of public rows with Chelsea chairman Ken Bates.

Recent newspaper reports said Middleton believed Chelsea needed to give more boardroom influence to a director with financial kudos if the club were to maintain the confidence of investors after the death of Harding.
Chelsea Village shares were marked down 11 pence, just over 10 percent, to 96-1/2 on Thursday, although no trades were reported by 1600 GMT
